ai_note: Design, specifications and testing by the author; code written with the assistance of AI tools.
all_clean_desc: There are no activity traces to remove in your home folder.
app_subtitle: Removes activity traces from your home folder: thumbnails, recent files, histories, clipboard, search index and trash.
confirm_caveat: This is an ordinary delete, not a secure wipe. The data may still be recoverable from the device, from filesystem snapshots and from backups.
confirm_dry: Simulation is on: nothing will actually be removed.
done_errors: Done. Freed {size}; {count} item(s) could not be removed.
dry_banner: Simulation is on: nothing will be removed
err_home_owner: The home folder {path} does not belong to the current user. RuscaCleaner will not delete anything there.
err_no_gtk: The window requires GTK 4 and libadwaita 1.7 or later. Use --list or --dry-run to work without a desktop.
err_root: RuscaCleaner cleans your own home folder and refuses to run as root. Start it as your normal user.
limits_body:
It removes files without overwriting them: a forensic tool, a btrfs snapshot or a backup may still hold the contents.
It does not touch browser data, the system journal, GNOME Shell app usage statistics or the settings of individual applications.
It deliberately keeps ~/.ssh/known_hosts and ~/.wget-hsts, because they protect your connections.
log_dry: Simulation: the lines below show what would be removed.
log_skip_is_home: skipped, this is the home folder itself: {path}
log_skip_symlink: skipped, it is a symbolic link: {path}
note_clipboard: The clipboard manager also keeps its history in memory: clear it from its menu too, or restart it.
note_gvfs: The file manager may need to be restarted before the change is visible.
note_recent: Open applications keep this list in memory and write it again when they quit: close them first, or expect some entries to come back.
note_search: GNOME rebuilds the search index by itself. Log out and back in afterwards: until then the indexer keeps the old database open.
note_shell: An open session rewrites its history on exit: close the terminals too, or run history -c in each one.
note_tools: Programs write their history again when they quit: close them before cleaning.
note_volume_trash: Removable and secondary drives keep their own trash. Only drives mounted right now can be cleaned.
